chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who had entered into iḥrām for Hajj al-Ifrād. When he entered Makkah, he performed tawāf of the House, then went to his companions while they were shortening their hair, so he shortened with them. Then, after he had shortened, he remembered that he was performing Hajj al-Ifrād.
So he عليه السلام said: “There is nothing upon him. When he has prayed, then let him renew the talbiyah.”

key_terms.أَفْرَدَ الْحَجَّ: entered into Hajj al-Ifrād, performing hajj in the ifrād form
key_terms.فَلْيُجَدِّدِ التَّلْبِيَةَ: let him renew the talbiyah to continue the hajj rite
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: no penalty, liability, or expiation is upon him
key_terms.مُفْرِدٌ لِلْحَجِّ: one who is in the state of performing Hajj al-Ifrād

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Ifrād mistakenly shortens his hair in Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Ifrād who mistakenly shortened his hair in Makkah as though he were exiting iḥrām. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that no penalty is due upon him, and that after performing salat, he should renew the talbiyah. The narration reflects the precision of Shia fiqh in correcting ritual mistakes during hajj.
